correctness.rationale: Orthogonal covariance reduces the Frobenius norm to the radial axis without using the target theorem. The Lyons–Zumbrun identity then shows that a component vanishes if any transverse multiplicity is odd; for even transverse multiplicities it factors as a product of odd double factorials times a one-dimensional derivative of an iterate of D. Summing with the exact multinomial multiplicity gives a central-binomial convolution whose generating function is (1-z)^(-(d-1)/2), yielding exactly the published coefficient. The origin follows by smooth extension and continuity. Checks at orders two and three agree with the focal source; finite symbolic checks were only sanity checks.

value.rationale: The focal paper explicitly identifies this derivation as an open problem. The solution is not a cosmetic reproof: it gives a transparent component classification on a radial axis and explains the coefficient product as a central-binomial convolution. This both answers the stated question and supplies a compact combinatorial interpretation of the all-order coefficients that is useful when manipulating radial higher derivatives.
